timeline: You might assume a 329-meter stone dam would instantly sink into loose riverbed sand, but how did King Karikala keep it standing since 150 CE?
King Karikala built the unhewn stone dam right across running water.
But the king dropped rough boulders straight into running water.
The dam diverted the waters of the Kaveri across the fertile delta region for irrigation.
It diverted raging floods across sixty-nine thousand acres of parched delta land.
British engineers studied it in eighteen-hundred and four.
They found it still diverting water after seventeen centuries of monsoon floods.
How did King Karikala build the 329-meter Kallanai stone dam on quicksand in 150 CE without modern machinery?
